summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, and atrial fibrillation was admitted with a one-week history of productive cough and acute chest pain. He presented from dialysis with dyspnea and low-grade fever. Chest imaging revealed a new right middle lobe infiltrate concerning for pneumonia and mild pulmonary edema. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics initially, then transitioned to oral levofloxacin with clinical improvement. Chest pain, likely musculoskeletal from coughing, resolved during the stay. Troponin was mildly elevated but stable, without ECG changes, suggesting no acute coronary syndrome. He completed a scheduled hemodialysis session and remained on his baseline medications, including omeprazole for recent esophagitis. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with his outpatient team.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
